funding_types.quote: All loans are repayable and have competitive interest rates and repayment terms.

max_amount.text: Up to $150,000 per borrower (more in some cases)
max_amount.quote: CBDC offers up to $150,000* per qualified borrower.

criteria.text: A rural business in Atlantic Canada (which includes Newfoundland and Labrador)
criteria.quote: Rural based businesses across Atlantic Canada meeting the following criteria may qualify for CBDC’s Innovation Loan:

criteria.text: The money buys equipment or software that is new technology (training staff on it may also count)
criteria.quote: CBDC Innovation Loans can be used to finance any costs of the purchase of equipment, software, processes, licenses, and other items that are clearly identifiable as “new” technology that will enhance the business.

criteria.text: What you buy is clearly new technology that will improve the business
criteria.quote: CBDC Innovation Loans can be used to finance any costs of the purchase of equipment, software, processes, licenses, and other items that are clearly identifiable as “new” technology that will enhance the business.

criteria.text: Both the business and the borrower are in rural areas
criteria.quote: Both the business and the borrower must be located in rural areas;

criteria.text: The business has realistic prospects of economic viability
criteria.quote: The business should have a realistic prospects of economic viability.

criteria.text: Your local CBDC offers this loan (programs vary by region)
criteria.quote: Programs and services delivered by CBDCs may vary by region.

research.notes: Purpose: the page names equipment, software, processes and licences that are new technology, so equipment and digital; it never mentions research, so research is not in the rule (gm2 K1). Training is unclear: the page says the loan 'could also be used for financing for new products or services and training' and covers training staff who work with the new technology, but not training on its own. The "clearly new technology" condition is check-this-yourself because ordinary equipment would also show met. The page says CBDCs may offer financing above $150,000 in certain situations. Intake: not stated. Contacts: the offices of CBDC Central (Grand Falls-Windsor), CBDC Gander Area and CBDC Emerald (Baie Verte, with a Springdale satellite office), each quoted from its own cbdc.ca office page saved as a source of this record; all three pages list this loan. Only the Gander Area page names the places it serves (a list of place names, not census divisions), so census_divisions is null for every office and there is no location rule beyond the province (contract question B). Other CBDCs in the province are not listed as contacts. Each office page says "In rural Newfoundland and Labrador there are 15 Corporations dedicated to the development of small business and job creation", so the labels give the office's town and "one of 15 CBDCs in the province" (gm2 K3, DECISIONS #23): an owner elsewhere should call their local CBDC.
